# codex — cortex context integration

**Layer:** `mcp`  ·  **Status:** `documented`  ·  **Surface:** `~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers]`

This harness reads MCP servers from its own configuration, so it needs **no shim**. Registration is a config entry.

## Why this layer

MCP-native; registration is a config entry, no shim.

## Install

```bash
Add to ~/.codex/config.toml:
  [mcp_servers.cortex-context]
  command = "python3"
  args = ["<mcp_server>"]
```

## Verify (do not report a wiring you have not exercised)

1. codex mcp list shows cortex-context
2. Call mem_context; the peer card must come back.

## Session identity

One session = one identity. Precedence is identical in every layer (args → env → git), which is what lets a checkpoint written here be restored by another harness.

```bash
export CORTEX_SESSION_HARNESS=<value>
export CORTEX_SESSION_REPO=<value>
export CORTEX_SESSION_BRANCH=<value>
```

Overrides (usually unnecessary, needed on macOS):

```bash
export CORTEX_CONTEXT_CLI=<path>   # see the failure modes in the runbook
export CORTEX_CONTEXT_PYTHON=<path>   # see the failure modes in the runbook
```

## Shared pieces (identical for every harness — never fork them)

- CLI: `~/.hermes-cortex/scripts/cortex-context.py`
- MCP server: `~/hermes-cortex/mcp-servers/cortex-context-mcp.py`
- Trigger: `~/.hermes-cortex/scripts/session-autocheckpoint.py`
- One implementation: `ops/services/mycortex-mem/context_tools.py`

Full runbook: [`docs/runbooks/context-integration.md`](../../../docs/runbooks/context-integration.md)
